run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:00:21Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is a propagated symptom: the Deployment otel-demo/ad was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-16T13:01:41Z (template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt), the single warmed-up ad pod was replaced by a cold one, and the new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was CPU-throttled in 95-99% of CFS periods because the ad container has limits cpu=50m and no readiness/liveness probe. While the new pod was reported Ready and the old pod was deleted 2 seconds after the new container started, the ad app could not accept connections: frontend's gRPC client spans to oteldemo.AdService/GetAds failed with '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' (the ad ClusterIP), and ad's own GetAds span rate fell to zero in metric windows ending 13:05:21-13:10:21. frontend therefore returned 500 on /api/data and hung on some ad calls (one sampled trace: 24.6 s frontend /api/data span, 22.4 s ad server span), so frontend-proxy returned 500 (via_upstream), 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started and 504 UT response_timeout (15000 ms) against upstream frontend, which drove its error rate from ~0 to 2.05/s and fired the alert. Recovery followed the CFS throttling curve: ad throttling fell to 0.63 by 13:13:21 and ~0.26-0.30 after 13:15, frontend ad-call errors stopped by 13:12:21 and frontend-proxy's ERROR rate returned to ~0.01-0.02/s by 13:15:21-13:19:21. frontend-proxy itself was unchanged and healthy as a process; the other frontend gRPC dependencies (ProductCatalogService, CartService, CheckoutService, RecommendationService) recorded zero ERROR spans.

claims.text: In 12:00:21-13:24:21 the frontend-proxy span metrics recorded 427.19 ERROR spans on span_name="ingress" (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and 393.71 ERROR spans on span_name="router frontend egress" (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), against 24393.5 and 24426.0 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans respectively.
frontend-proxy's ERROR span rate (rate over 5m) was ~0 at 12:41:21-12:53:21, rose to 0.40/s at 13:03:21, peaked at 2.05/s at 13:07:21, and was back to 0.0148/s at 13:15:21 and 0.0209/s at 13:19:21.

frontend-proxy's own access logs show request errors against upstream frontend (100.67.43.114:8080) between 13:08:45 and 13:11:09: 'GET /api/data...' 500 - via_upstream; 'GET /api/products/...' 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}; and 'GET /api/data...' 504 UT response_timeout with 15000 ms upstream time. By 13:12:29-13:12:32 the same proxy logged 200 via_upstream responses.

frontend's own span metrics for the whole window show 393.46 ERROR spans on span_name="GET /api/data" (SERVER), 393.46 on "executing api route (pages) /api/data", 393.46 on SERVER "GET", and 393.62 on CLIENT "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds"; the same query shows 0 ERROR spans for CLIENT grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations.

frontend's failing gRPC client spans to oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carry the exact error '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' (grpc.error_message on span tag, rpc.grpc.status_code=14), and the same message appears on the parent 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' spans; 100.70.197.56:8080 is the ClusterIP:port of Service ad in namespace otel-demo.

Per-2m increases: frontend's AdService/GetAds ERROR count went from 0 at 13:02:21 to 65.3 at 13:03:21, 140-158.7 at 13:04:21-13:05:21, 133-152 at 13:07:21-13:08:21, 86.7 at 13:10:21, 20 at 13:11:21 and 0 at 13:12:21, while its UNSET count fell to 0 in windows ending 13:05:21-13:09:21; ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server span increase was 0 in windows ending 13:05:21 through 13:10:21 and resumed at 82.98 at 13:11:21.

Deployment ad was deliberately rolled out at 13:01:41Z: its pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:01:41Z, metadata.generation=2 and revision 2; ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 was created 13:01:41 with pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 was scaled 1->0 and pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was killed/deleted at 13:01:43 (SuccessfulDelete), and the new pod's ad container started at 13:01:43 with restartCount 0.

The ad container spec has resources.limits cpu=50m and memory=450Mi, requests cpu=10m and memory=225Mi, no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe, with strategy RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%.

The new ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was CPU-throttled for 0.95-0.99 of CFS periods from 13:02:21 through 13:10:21, 0.875 at 13:11:21, 0.756 at 13:12:21, 0.629 at 13:13:21, 0.402 at 13:14:21 and ~0.26-0.30 from 13:15:21 to 13:19:21, whereas the previous ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc had been throttled only 0.082-0.125 in 12:55:21-13:05:21.

ad's own server spans reported no errors: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had 1495.95 STATUS_CODE_UNSET and 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, and ad's duration histogram for GetAds (total 1495.95) contains very few slow samples above 1000 ms (1489.25 at le=1000). ad's container logs from 13:10:41 to 13:12:31 show normal 'Targeted ad request received' / 'Non-targeted ad request received' and 'no baggage found in context' lines.

Whole trace d4057d2e24ea083d01006c39cd8fcd6a (start 13:09:02) shows the slow-path propagation: load-generator GET span 15.31 s with error=true http.status_code=504 -> frontend-proxy ingress 15.00 s 504 and router frontend egress 15.00 s http.status_code=0 -> frontend GET /api/data 24.59 s (http.status_code=200) -> frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 24.59 s rpc.grpc.status_code=0 -> ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 22.37 s, with ad's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans of 1.6 s, 3.6 s and 2.3 s at rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and a flagd server span with otel.status_description 'context deadline exceeded'.

ad recorded no ERROR span status of its own (1.02 errored spans only on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, ResolveBoolean errors 0 across all minutes) and its logs contain request-served lines without errors, so ad did not fail by reporting application errors; the observed ad-side failure mode is CPU starvation/unavailability plus multi-second latency, not ad error statuses.

frontend and frontend-proxy were not restarted or redeployed: frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw was created 12:29:37 and frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-kxdcl 12:29:35, both with restartCount 0 and container startedAt 12:29:40, and neither Deployment carries a restartedAt annotation (frontend Deployment generation 1).

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready with the expected restart counts (only fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 showed 1 restart), and all 21 Deployments reported readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1, updatedReplicas=1 at query time.

Only two Deployments in otel-demo carry a kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt template annotation: ad at 2026-11-16T13:01:41Z (revision 2) and flagd at 2026-11-16T12:31:27Z (revision 2); all other Deployments have none.

The flagd-related ERROR spans observed in the window are only long-lived EventStream errors: ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.33 at 12:57:21-12:58:21, fraud-detection EventStream 1.33 at 13:00:21-13:01:21, recommendation /flagd...EventStream 1.33 in four separate 2m windows (12:52:21, 13:02:21, 13:11:21, 13:13:21); recommendation's only ERROR spans (4.06 total) and fraud-detection's (1.02 total) are these flagd EventStream spans.

Primary cause: the 13:01:41Z rollout restart of Deployment ad replaced the single warmed-up ad replica with a cold one whose Java process could not get enough CPU under limits.cpu=50m (CFS throttling 0.95-0.99), and because the container has no readiness probe the replacement pod was marked Ready and the old pod was deleted 2 s after the new container started, so the ad Service ClusterIP 100.70.197.56:8080 refused connections and served requests only very slowly until the throttling eased around 13:11.

frontend-proxy is a victim, not the faulting component: its pod and Deployment were unchanged, and every one of its observed error log lines (500 via_upstream, 503 upstream_reset_before_response_started, 504 response_timeout) is attributable to upstream frontend 100.67.43.114:8080, whose /api/data handler was blocked on the ad dependency.

Secondary, unconfirmed contributor: flagd may have been slow at ~13:09 (ad's flagd ResolveBoolean client spans hit rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and flagd's own server span says 'context deadline exceeded'), which could have stretched ad's already CPU-starved GetAds handling; however flagd was restarted 30 minutes earlier at 12:31:27, its pod is Running with 0 restarts, and the corresponding ResolveBoolean error metric for ad is 0, so flagd's role is not established.

Add a readiness probe (and a liveness probe) to the ad container so a not-yet-listening ad pod is never added to the Service Endpoints and the old pod is not terminated before the replacement can serve; for a single-replica Deployment also consider maxUnavailable=0 with maxSurge=1 so the warmed-up replica stays until the new one is actually ready.

Review the ad container CPU quota: limits.cpu=50m (requests 10m) produced 95-99% CFS throttling of the fresh pod versus ~10% on the long-running pod; raise the startup CPU allocation (or remove the tight limit) so JVM/OTel-agent start-up fits before traffic is routed.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (no rule named RequestErrorRate, and a label match on alertname=RequestErrorRate returned nothing), so the alert expression and the reported value 2.4555555555555553 could not be verified against the rule.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart on Deployment ad at 2026-11-16T13:01:41Z, and whether a configuration change accompanied it, is unknown.

frontend container logs could not be read (current and previous streams returned 0 bytes), so frontend's own application-level error lines (e.g. the AdService exception text) are unknown; the frontend error evidence comes from spans only.

The ad container log history appears truncated: only 340 lines were readable and the earliest available line is 13:10:41, so logs cannot establish when the new ad process began listening; the unavailability window rests on span metrics and CPU-throttling metrics instead.

flagd container logs could not be read (0 bytes for init-config, flagd and flagd-ui) and no span-metric series exist for service_name="flagd", so whether flagd was slow or unhealthy at ~13:09 cannot be confirmed or excluded.

kube-state-metrics pod readiness series (kube_pod_container_info and similar) returned no series in the window, so the new ad pod's readiness transition is inferred from Deployment/ReplicaSet events and the absence of a readiness probe, not observed directly.
No node-level data (node conditions, node CPU pressure on i-040b429451d033123) was examined; a node-side contributor to the throttling cannot be fully excluded from this investigation.

Trace data is a sampled view (traces_search returned 292 error spans, of which 40 were read; traces cover roughly 12:52-13:14) and Jaeger retains only the most recent 5000 traces, so span counts here are not unique request counts or a complete call graph.

The rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count metric has no series for service_name frontend or ad, and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count has no frontend-proxy series, so those alternative error/latency indicators could not corroborate the span metrics.
next_steps: Confirm from audit/change history who or what triggered the ad Deployment rollout restart at 2026-11-16T13:01:41Z and whether the pod template spec (image, env, resources) changed in that revision.
Add a readiness probe and raise the ad container CPU limit in the Deployment manifest, then verify by a controlled rollout that a new ad pod serves before the old pod is removed.
Check the alerting rule definition for RequestErrorRate in the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration to confirm which metric and threshold produced the 2.4555 value for frontend-proxy.
If flagd-related latency recurs, enable or retain flagd span metrics and logs so ad's flagd ResolveBoolean deadline errors can be distinguished from ad-side CPU starvation.
